_comment: Local knowledge pack. Two distinct jobs:
token expansion in Stage 2 scoring. Without synonym expansion, dept_stat -> isActive
has literally zero lexical overlap and would never reach the shortlist.
2. 'snippets' are retrieved (3-5 per batch) and injected into Stage 3 prompts, giving
the model an authority to cite in its reasoning instead of inventing one.
Small enough to stay in memory; a vector database for this corpus would cost more
per month than the entire pipeline costs to run.

type_map.note: MongoDB generates _id; keep the legacy integer for traceability.
Resolve through an ID remap table built during migration.
Number is a double; use Decimal128 if exact currency arithmetic is required.
Requires a value lookup from single-character codes to readable strings.
Lossy: collapses a multi-state code into two states.
MySQL boolean integer idiom maps to a native Boolean.
Date-only value becomes midnight UTC; confirm the intended timezone.
MySQL DATETIME carries no timezone; assume UTC unless the source says otherwise.

snippets.text: ISO 4217 currency codes are exactly three uppercase letters (USD, GBP, JPY). A CHAR(3) currency column maps to a String with no value transform; validate against the ISO list.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes are two uppercase letters (US, GB, JP). A CHAR(2) country column maps to a String unchanged.
IANA timezone identifiers look like Area/Location (America/Los_Angeles). Store as String verbatim; never convert to a UTC offset, which loses daylight-saving rules.
Legacy MySQL uses snake_case; the MongoDB target uses camelCase. A trailing _cd means code, _nm means name, _dt means date, _ts means timestamp, and an is_ prefix means a boolean flag.
MySQL has no native boolean; TINYINT(1) with values 0 and 1 is the idiom. It maps to a MongoDB Boolean with 0 to false and 1 to true.
Single-character CHAR(1) status codes require a lookup transform to readable enum strings, and the legend is usually documented in the column comment.

A relational INT primary key maps to MongoDB _id, but ObjectId values are generated by MongoDB rather than carried over. Retain the original integer in a legacy field so foreign keys can be resolved during migration.
A relational foreign key maps to an ObjectId reference field. The migration needs an ID remap table from legacy integer keys to generated ObjectIds, applied after the referenced collection is loaded.

Document stores often denormalize a joined label alongside its reference, for example department.code and department.name next to department.departmentId. Those copies have no counterpart column in the referencing table; they are populated by joining the referenced table during migration.
DECIMAL(12,2) is exact; the MongoDB Number type is an IEEE 754 double and is not. For monetary values prefer Decimal128, or store minor units as an integer.
Legacy created_ts and updated_ts audit columns conventionally move into a meta sub-document as createdAt and updatedAt.
MySQL DATETIME has no timezone. MongoDB ISODate is always UTC, so the migration must state the assumed source timezone; assuming UTC without checking silently shifts every timestamp.
